evidence.claim: The 2022 Government Work Report set targets of around 5.5 percent GDP growth, over 11 million new urban jobs, stable macroeconomic performance, deeper reform, higher-standard opening up, innovation, and improved wellbeing.
evidence.title: China releases full text of Government Work Report
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 Government Work Report set targets of around 5.5 percent GDP growth, over 11 million new urban jobs, stable macroeconomic performance, deeper reform, higher-standard opening up, innovation, and improved wellbeing.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government program text is strong for announced intent and policy direction, but weaker on realized effect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but material. It was delivered by Premier Li Keqiang for the Xi-led State Council, so it reflects top-state economic direction rather than Xi's sole authorship.
contrary_evidence: The report is aspirational and does not itself show implementation.
Actual 2022 growth later landed well below the 5.5 percent target.

evidence.claim: Xi said China should pursue high-quality development, improve the distribution system, widen high-standard opening-up, strengthen innovation and talent policy, and make progress toward common prosperity.
evidence.title: Xi Jinping's report to the 20th National Congress of the CPC
evidence.excerpt: Xi said China should pursue high-quality development, improve the distribution system, widen high-standard opening-up, strengthen innovation and talent policy, and make progress toward common prosperity.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct Xi-authored strategic report is strong for stated intent and self-assessed trajectory, though it remains a self-report.
evidence.period_fit: Target-period strategic address delivered Oct. 16, 2022 and published Oct. 25, 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi as party leader and principal speaker.
contrary_evidence: This is a self-report and mixes aspiration with retrospective claims.
Independent macro sources still described serious slowdown, property stress, and policy uncertainty in 2022.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Xi secured a third term and unveiled a new leadership team dominated by allies, including the entire seven-member Politburo Standing Committee.
evidence.title: Factbox-China's new political elites and their connection to Xi
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Xi secured a third term and unveiled a new leadership team dominated by allies, including the entire seven-member Politburo Standing Committee.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters factbox is strong contemporaneous reporting on elite composition and political control.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi because it concerns his chosen top team and the consolidation of his personal network.
contrary_evidence: Some new officials were technocrats, not pure ideologues.
A loyalist-heavy team does not by itself prove economic incompetence, only reduced independence.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said China's growth was expected to slow to 2.7 percent in 2022 amid pandemic disruptions and real-estate stress, and it called for deeper structural reforms, predictable regulation, better credit access, and more support for youth employment.
evidence.title: China Economic Update - December 2022
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said China's growth was expected to slow to 2.7 percent in 2022 amid pandemic disruptions and real-estate stress, and it called for deeper structural reforms, predictable regulation, better credit access, and more support for youth employment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: High-quality independent macro assessment with explicit policy recommendations and date fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is not a Xi-only causal finding, but it is strong independent context for the Xi-era policy environment and the consequences of those choices.
contrary_evidence: It is a forecast and policy recommendation, not a direct ruling on Xi's intent.
Part of the slowdown also came from global shocks and pandemic dynamics.

evidence.claim: IMF staff said China's 2022 growth would be below global growth for the first time in over 40 years, with zero-COVID restrictions, the deep property-sector contraction, and weak global demand weighing on the economy, and it described support for unfinished housing and mortgage relief among the policy responses.
evidence.title: People's Republic of China: 2022 Article IV Consultation
evidence.excerpt: IMF staff said China's 2022 growth would be below global growth for the first time in over 40 years, with zero-COVID restrictions, the deep property-sector contraction, and weak global demand weighing on the economy, and it described support for unfinished housing and mortgage relief among the policy responses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent macro surveillance with clear causation analysis and detailed policy discussion.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective 2022 IMF surveillance published after the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Not direct personal attribution, but it strongly assesses the Xi-led policy regime and its macro consequences.
contrary_evidence: This is staff analysis, not a binding legal finding.
The IMF also recognizes that some support measures were introduced in response.

evidence.claim: The NBS reported that real per-capita disposable income rose 2.9 percent in 2022, rural income grew faster than urban income, and real per-capita consumption fell 0.2 percent, with the median income still below the mean.
evidence.title: Households' Income and Consumption Expenditure in 2022
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China
evidence.excerpt: The NBS reported that real per-capita disposable income rose 2.9 percent in 2022, rural income grew faster than urban income, and real per-capita consumption fell 0.2 percent, with the median income still below the mean.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary household survey release with detailed distributional measures, though still official data.
evidence.period_fit: Full-year 2022 household outcomes published immediately after year end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level household outcomes are only partially attributable to Xi, but they are the best official evidence of household welfare under his 2022 rule.
contrary_evidence: Urban households' real income growth was only 1.9 percent and real consumption fell.
The release does not isolate ruler-specific causality from pandemic and macro conditions.

evidence.claim: China's 2022 R&D spending reached 30,782.9 billion yuan, up 10.1 percent year on year, with intensity at 2.54 percent of GDP and basic research growing 11.4 percent.
evidence.title: 2022 National R&D Expenditure Statistics Bulletin
evidence.publisher: National Bureau of Statistics of China / Ministry of Science and Technology / Ministry of Finance
evidence.excerpt: China's 2022 R&D spending reached 30,782.9 billion yuan, up 10.1 percent year on year, with intensity at 2.54 percent of GDP and basic research growing 11.4 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary statistical bulletin with a clear full-year investment measure, though subject to official-data caveats.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects Xi-era priorities for technology and innovation, though the R&D system is also shaped by ministries, firms, and provinces.
contrary_evidence: Higher R&D spending does not guarantee efficient allocation or broad prosperity.
It does not by itself prove that innovation policy improved household welfare in 2022.

evidence.claim: Officials said financial supervision had been tightened, more than 124 stockholders who breached laws or regulations had been disclosed, and corruption behind financial risks had been investigated and punished.
evidence.title: Press conference on reform and development of China's financial sector since the 18th CPC National Congress
evidence.excerpt: Officials said financial supervision had been tightened, more than 124 stockholders who breached laws or regulations had been disclosed, and corruption behind financial risks had been investigated and punished.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official account with concrete enforcement figures, but it is still a self-justifying report from the sector it describes.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year 2022 press conference summarizing the Xi era and ongoing 2022 reform posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Xi-era party-state financial governance model, though specific cases were handled by regulators and discipline bodies.
contrary_evidence: This is an official self-report and may overstate effectiveness.
A crackdown can reflect political discipline as well as genuine anti-corruption.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 evidence of Xi's own assets, liabilities, outside interests, or a personal public correction/admission.
Most of the anti-corruption and data-fraud material is system-level enforcement, not proof of Xi's own candor or self-dealing.
The strongest family-wealth context is pre-2022 and indirect, so its period fit for the target year is weak.
